arxiv-1706-06975.title: On the enumeration of sentences by compactness
arxiv-1706-06975.creator: Mark A. Stalzer
arxiv-1706-06975.description: Abstract Presented is a Julia meta-program that discovers compact theories from data if they exist. It writes candidate theories in Julia and then validates: tossing the bad theories and keeping the good theories. Compactness is measured by a metric: such as the number of space-time derivatives.

arxiv-2104-12805.title: Evidence for Ultra-Diffuse Galaxy Formation Through Tidal Heating of Normal Dwarfs Journal: ApJ Facilities: VLA, HST (ACS), Blanco, CFHT, GBO:300ft DOLPHOT ( Dolphin2000 ) , CASA ( CASA ) , astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ) , APLpy ( aplpy2012 ; aplpy2
arxiv-2104-12805.creator: MICHAEL G. JONES, PAUL BENNET, BURÇİN MUTLU-PAKDİL, DAVID J. SAND, KRISTINE SPEKKENS, DENIJA CRNOJEVIĆ, ANANTHAN KARUNAKARAN, DENNIS ZARITSKY
arxiv-2104-12805.description: Abstract We have followed up two ultra-diffuse galaxies (UDGs), detected adjacent to stellar streams, with Hubble Space Telescope (HST) imaging and H i mapping with the Jansky Very Large Array (VLA) in order to investigate the possibility that they might have a tidal origin.

arxiv-2209-03089.title: Decoding Demographic un- fairness from Indian Names
arxiv-2209-03089.creator: Medidoddi Vahini, Jalend Bantupalli, Souvic Chakraborty, Animesh Mukherjee
arxiv-2209-03089.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Medidoddi Vahini, Jalend Bantupalli, Souvic Chakraborty, Animesh Mukherjee. Demographic classification is essential in fairness assessment in recommender systems or in measuring unintended bias in online networks and voting systems. Important fields like education and politics, which often lay a foundation for the future of equality in society, need scrutiny to design policies that can better foster equality in resource distribution constrained by the unbalanced demographic distribution of people in the country.

arxiv-2309-10967.title: Concentration Dependence of Elastic and Viscoelastic Properties of Aqueous Solutions of Ficoll and Bovine Serum Albumin by Brillouin Light Scattering Spectroscopy
arxiv-2309-10967.creator: Stephen J. Spencer, Venketesh Thrithamara Ranganathan, Anand Yethiraj, and G. Todd Andrews
arxiv-2309-10967.description: Abstract The cellular environment is crowded with macromolecules of different shapes and sizes. The effect of this macromolecular crowding has been studied in a variety of synthetic crowding environments: two popular examples are the compact colloid-like Ficoll macromolecule, and the globular protein bovine serum albumin (BSA).

arxiv-2406-08504.title: NONCOMMUTATIVE DONOHO-STARK-ELAD-BRUCKSTEIN-RICAUD-TORRÉSANI UNCERTAINTY PRINCIPLE
arxiv-2406-08504.creator: K. MAHESH KRISHNA
arxiv-2406-08504.description: Abstract Abstract : Let \{\tau_{n}\}_{n=1}^{\infty} and \{\omega_{m}\}_{m=1}^{\infty} be two modular Parseval frames for a Hilbert C*-module \mathcal{E} . Then for every x\in\mathcal{E}\setminus\{0\} , we show that (1) \displaystyle\|\theta_{\tau}x\|_{0}\|\theta_{\omega}x\|_{0}\geq\frac{1}{\sup_{n,m\in\mathbb{N}}\|\langle\tau_{n},\omega_{m}\rangle\|^{2}}. We call Inequality ( 1 ) as Noncommutative Donoho-Stark-Elad-Bruckstein-Ricaud-Torrésani Uncertainty Principle . Inequality ( 1 ) is the noncommutative analogue of breakthrough Ricaud-Torrésani uncertainty principle [IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory, 2013] .

arxiv-2407-10544.title: Port-Hamiltonian Modeling and Control of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations
arxiv-2407-10544.creator: Hannes Gernandt, Bernardo Severino ‡, Xinyi Zhang ‡, Volker Mehrmann, Kai Strunz
arxiv-2407-10544.description: Abstract Electric vehicles (EV) are an important part of future sustainable transportation. The increasing integration of EV charging stations (EVCSs) in the existing power grids require new scaleable control algorithms that maintain the stability and resilience of the grid. Here, we present such a control approach using an averaged port-Hamiltonian model.

arxiv-2410-16832.title: Zeta functions of orders on surfaces Thanks: The authors were supported by the Australian Research Council Discovery Project grant DP220102861
arxiv-2410-16832.creator: Daniel Chan, Sean Lynch

arxiv-2412-00950.title: Subsweep: Extensions to the sweep method for radiative transfer
arxiv-2412-00950.creator: Toni Peter, Joseph S. W. Lewis, Ralf S. Klessen, Simon C. O. Glover, Guido Kanschat
arxiv-2412-00950.description: Abstract We introduce the radiative transfer postprocessing code Subsweep . The code is based on the method of transport sweeps, in which the exact solution to the scattering-less radiative transfer equation is computed in a single pass through the entire computational grid.

arxiv-2505-23673.title: Bayesian Optimization from Human Feedback: Near-Optimal Regret Bounds
arxiv-2505-23673.creator: Aya Kayal, Sattar Vakili, Laura Toni, Da-shan Shiu, Alberto Bernacchia
arxiv-2505-23673.description: Abstract Bayesian optimization (BO) with preference-based feedback has recently garnered significant attention due to its emerging applications. We refer to this problem as Bayesian Optimization from Human Feedback (BOHF), which differs from conventional BO by learning the best actions from a reduced feedback model, where only the preference between two actions is revealed to the learner at each time step.

arxiv-2506-20688.title: Building Lightweight Semantic Segmentation Models for Aerial Images Using Dual Relation Distillation
arxiv-2506-20688.creator: Minglong Li, Lianlei Shan, Weiqiang Wang, Ke Lv, Bin Luo, Si-Bao Chen
arxiv-2506-20688.description: Abstract Recently, there have been significant improvements in the accuracy of CNN models for semantic segmentation. However, these models are often heavy and suffer from low inference speed, which limits their practical application. To address this issue, knowledge distillation has emerged as a promising approach to achieve a good trade-off between segmentation accuracy and efficiency.

arxiv-2510-18206.title: Adaptive Per-Channel Energy Normalization Front-end for Robust Audio Signal Processing
arxiv-2510-18206.creator: Hanyu Meng, Vidhyasaharan Sethu, Eliathamby Ambikairajah, Qiquan Zhang, Haizhou Li
arxiv-2510-18206.description: Abstract In audio signal processing, learnable front-ends have shown strong performance across diverse tasks by optimizing task-specific representation. However, their parameters remain fixed once trained, lacking flexibility during inference and limiting robustness under dynamic complex acoustic environments. In this paper, we introduce a novel adaptive paradigm for audio front-ends that replaces static parameterization with a closed-loop neural controller.

arxiv-2510-25927.title: Constraints on the resolution of spacetime singularities
arxiv-2510-25927.creator: Arvin Shahbazi-Moghaddam
arxiv-2510-25927.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Arvin Shahbazi-Moghaddam. What happens at spacetime singularities is poorly understood. The Penrose–Wall singularity theorem constrains possible scenarios, but until recently its key assumption—the generalized second law (GSL)—had only been proven perturbatively, severely limiting this application. We highlight that recent progress enables a proof of the GSL in holographic brane-world models, valid non-perturbatively at the species scale c ​ G cG (with c c the number of matter fields and G G Newton’s constant).

pmc-11353807.title: Consumer Perception of the Performance of Online Catering Food Safety Regulations: The Case of Shanghai, China
pmc-11353807.creator: Weijun Liu, Yige Wu, Yue Sun, Wojciech J Florkowski, Angelina Lopes Simoes Pena, Sofia Cancela Duarte
pmc-11353807.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). To protect the safety of food bought from the online catering sector, the former State Food and Drug Administration of China issued two separate regulations in 2016 and 2017. Independently, the Shanghai government formulated local regulations, including the Shanghai Online Catering Service Supervision and Management Measures, to strengthen food safety supervision in this megacity with the largest catering sector in China.

pmc-11426316.title: Mislabeled and ambiguous market names in invertebrate and finfish seafood conceal species of conservation concern in Calgary, Alberta, Canada
pmc-11426316.creator: Matthew R. J. Morris, Mindi M. Summers, Morgan Kwan, Jonathan A. Mee, Sean M. Rogers
pmc-11426316.description: BackgroundThe mislabeling of seafood, wherein a food product’s marketed name does not match its contents, has the potential to mask species of conservation concern. Less discussed is the role of legally ambiguous market names, wherein a single name could be used to sell multiple species.

pmc-11634843.title: Case Report: Concurrent de novo pathogenic variants in the LMNA gene as a cause of sporadic partial lipodystrophy
pmc-11634843.creator: José L. Santos, José Patricio Miranda, Carlos F. Lagos, Víctor A. Cortés
pmc-11634843.description: IntroductionInherited lipodystrophies are a group of rare diseases defined by severe reduction in adipose tissue mass and classified as generalized or partial. We report a non-familial (sporadic) case of partial lipodystrophy caused by a novel genetic mechanism involving closely linked de novo pathogenic variants in the LMNA gene.

pmc-11649498.title: TRPC6 is a Biomarker for Prognosis and Immunotherapy of Stomach Adenocarcinoma Based on Bioinformatic Analysis and Experimental Validation
pmc-11649498.creator: Xingchi Hu, Hongwei Wang, Haitao Sun, Jingxin Zhang, ZhenXiong Ye, Zhenhua Huang
pmc-11649498.description: BackgroundTransient receptor potential canonical 6 (TRPC6), a key member of the TRPC family, is involved in diverse physiological and pathological processes. Although previous studies have implicated TRPC6 in the progression of stomach adenocarcinoma (STAD), its precise functions and mechanisms remain unclear. Understanding TRPC6’s role in STAD may provide insights into its prognostic and therapeutic potential.

pmc-12640335.title: Determinants of ICU memories and the impact on the development and trajectory of post-traumatic stress symptoms: a multicenter longitudinal cohort study
pmc-12640335.creator: Rens W J Kooken, Bram Tilburgs, Arjen J C Slooter, Mark van den Boogaard
pmc-12640335.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). pmc-12641783.title: Modafinil for Promoting Wakefulness in Critically Ill Patients: Current Evidence and Perspectives
pmc-12641783.creator: Sotirios Kakavas, Dimitrios Karayiannis, Ramin Khatami
pmc-12641783.description: Critically ill patients are predisposed to developing cognitive dysfunction, excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS), and fatigue during their stay in the intensive care unit (ICU). Modafinil, a wakefulness-promoting agent, has demonstrated potential benefits in enhancing alertness, cognitive performance, and activity levels in various clinical populations.

pmc-13065979.title: A Bayesian perspective on observers’ inference of group norms
pmc-13065979.creator: Jipeng Duan, Xiuyan Guo, Li Zheng, Jun Yin
pmc-13065979.description: Inferring group norms is crucial for adapting behaviors in novel situations, but its underlying basis and computational account remain unclear. This study manipulated the prevalence of norm-consistent behaviors (i.e., straight-line movements) to examine whether and how norm inference is influenced by observed group behavior, exploring its consistency with Bayesian updating, robustness, and independence.

pmc-13095330.title: A nurse-led cross-sectional latent profile analysis of fear of cancer recurrence in patients with non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer
pmc-13095330.creator: Yuanting Hao, Linyan Niu, Yi-An Shih, Pengxia Gao, Yongcai Wu, Wanyan Song, Chong Li
pmc-13095330.description: To identify distinct latent profiles of fear of cancer recurrence (FCR) among patients with bladder cancer and to examine sociodemographic and modifiable psychosocial correlates (self-management and social support) from a nursing perspective. We conducted a nurse-led cross-sectional study of patients with non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer in northern China (August 2023–October 2024).

pmc-13120931.title: Relationship between depression, anxiety, and perceived burdensomeness: the mediating role of emotional regulation among Egyptian older adults
pmc-13120931.creator: Ibrahim Alasqah, Ahmed Abdelwahab Ibrahim El-Sayed, Ahmed Abdellah Othman, Mohamed Hussein Ramadan Atta, Noha Gamal El-Sayed Ghoniem, Shaimaa Mohamed Amin
pmc-13120931.description: ObjectiveTo examine whether emotion regulation moderates the relationship between depression, anxiety, and perceived burdensomeness among community-dwelling older adults with attention to its relevance for public health.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted among 300 adults aged ≥60 years attending outpatient clinics in Egypt. Validated instruments measured emotion regulation, depression, anxiety, and perceived burdensomeness.

pmc-13522410.title: People with borderline personality disorder experiences of mental health services in an Australian context: Associated anxiety and structural stigma
pmc-13522410.creator: Pauline Klein, Shahid Ullah, Sharon Lawn, A Kate Fairweather
pmc-13522410.description: Objective:The objective is to investigate associations between anxiety accessing mental health services and structural stigma as self-reported by people with borderline personality disorder.Methods:A retrospective cohort design was used to investigate data from the 2017 National Consumer Survey undertaken in Australia between June and July 2017. Analyses were performed using multivariate binary logistic regression models.
